Activities appears below Autopilot when an artifact has activity. It starts collapsed. Its heading shows the number of loaded activities, which increases when Earlier Activities loads older history. Use Enter or Space on its heading to expand it, then arrow keys to read the newest activity first. Scrolling past either end of the list scrolls the surrounding panel. Only rows with a chat destination respond to clicking or Enter; they reveal the related message. Other rows are informational. Pending actions offer Cancel Action, and uncertain outcomes offer Reconcile Outcome. The Accessible View includes the activity count and text.

Artifacts with enabled Autopilot rules have a trailing pill section with an Autopilot icon and the number of enabled rules. Select it to open and focus Autopilot. This count includes saved enabled rules even when new enablement is temporarily unavailable.

All Available Autopilot Rules applies only to its provider's currently available rules. The enabled count describes partial enablement. Enabling a group saves immediately and uses the policies shown in the dropdowns. Disabling a group revokes enabled rules without enabling unavailable ones.

Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between controls. Buttons below the state lists run actions once. Enabled actions come first in provider order, and the first action is primary. List rows show a single line; their full text and state remain available to screen readers and in hovers. Use Space to change an Autopilot switch. Enabling a rule grants permission for future automatic runs; it can run immediately if its condition already holds. Turning it off prevents new runs, but does not cancel work already started.

Descriptions show at most three lines. The Accessible View includes the full description. When a provider supplies more information about a list, use Tab to reach its information icon and Enter or Space to read the hover.

Escape or Close returns focus to the invoking pill. Clicking outside, including in the chat input, dismisses details without moving focus back. Clicking another artifact switches this panel; clicking its status section selects and focuses the corresponding list, or focuses its action.
A temporarily unavailable switch moves focus to its explanation, then back when available, unless you move focus elsewhere. Enabled automation remains available to turn off.

Artifact details show the full resource title and state icon, its description, tabbed state lists, actions, Autopilot, and Activities. Activate the linked title to open the resource. Copy Link and Remove Artifact are available in the footer.

State lists start collapsed. Clicking a state-list tab, or pressing Enter or Space on it, expands its list; activating the expanded tab again collapses all lists. While a list is expanded, Left and Right Arrow, Home, and End select another state-list tab and keep keyboard focus on the full tab; while all lists are collapsed, they only move focus between tabs. Clicking a tab moves focus to the first item in its list. Tab moves through the information buttons beside each tab label and into the expanded list. Enter or Space on an information button shows that list's details without selecting its tab. The list area keeps its height when you change tabs. Use arrow keys in a list and Enter to open its selected item. A pill's status section expands and focuses its list. Autopilot is collapsed by default; its heading expands or collapses its rules, and its separate switch enables all available rules or turns them off. Policy dropdowns remain visible while rules are off. Selecting a policy while off does not enable the rule; turning the switch on uses the displayed policy without asking again. Policy selections, expanded tabs, and Autopilot expansion choices are remembered when reopening the artifact.

To show or hide the aquarium action on the new-session view, use the checked Aquarium item in the context menu outside the composer, or run the Toggle Aquarium Action Visibility command.

To archive an individual nested chat without archiving its session, open the chat's context menu in the Sessions list or chat tab and choose Archive. The chat is hidden from the Sessions list and closed, but is not deleted. Open the Sessions list Filter menu and enable Archived to show it again, then open the chat's context menu and choose Unarchive.

When all GitHub pull requests associated with the session have merged and no chat is working or waiting for input, an archive suggestion may appear above the chat input. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Archive, Configure Automatic Cleanup, or Dismiss Archive Suggestion, then Enter or Space to activate it. Configure Automatic Cleanup opens the settings for automatically archiving inactive merged sessions and permanently deleting automatically archived merged sessions. The explanation under What Does "Archive" Do? is collapsed by default. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Dismiss Archive Suggestion, or Escape while the suggestion is focused, hides the suggestion for this session, including after a reload, until it is archived or deleted, and returns focus to the chat input. Archiving the session hides it from the sessions list so you can focus on your remaining tasks. The session is not deleted. Ask your agent to find it, or look in the "Archived" section of the sessions list. You can unarchive it anytime. The worktree created for the session, if any, will be deleted. You can recreate it by unarchiving the session.

Sending a new message after the suggestion appears hides it for those pull requests, including after a reload. It can appear again when a new pull request is added to the session and all its pull requests have merged.

The first time you activate the suggestion's Archive or Mark as Done button, a spotlight may reveal that session's action in the sessions list. It briefly waits for the list action to appear. The action waits until you activate the highlighted action, activate Understood, or press Escape to end the spotlight. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to move between the highlighted action and Understood, and Enter or Space to activate either. If the spotlight cannot be shown or is interrupted, the session is still archived or marked as done as long as the suggestion remains available. Once completed or skipped, the spotlight will not appear again.
To archive or mark one or more sessions as done, focus them in the Sessions list and invoke Archive or Mark as Done{0}.

Artifact actions appear as collapsed request cards with an action and resource label. Use Tab to reach the card and Enter or Space to expand it. The details are a snapshot from when the action started. Use arrow keys within a details list and Enter to open an item. Agent Message switches between these details and the full prompt. Open the accessible view{0} while the request is focused to read its snapshot as text.
If a focused automation control becomes temporarily unavailable, focus moves to its explanation and returns to the control when it becomes available, unless you have moved focus elsewhere.

In Agent Host sessions, enabling, changing, or disabling an artifact automation adds a notice to the chat that recorded the artifact. Notices explain what will run automatically and why a rule was turned off, including unsuccessful attempts that caused automatic disablement. Use Tab to reach the notice and Enter or Space to expand or collapse its details. Notices raised while the agent is working appear after that turn finishes. Automatic repair prompts appear as messages in that chat without replacing your draft.

Autopilot groups the opt-in rules for automatic actions. It starts collapsed. Activate its heading to expand the rules, or use its separate switch to enable all available rules or turn them off. The trailing artifact pill section shows the number of enabled Autopilot rules and opens this section.

The {0} setting enables live artifact details, actions, and Autopilot instead of Agent Merge. It is off by default. Switching pauses saved automation choices and stops automation-owned work without cancelling human-started work. Switching back can resume previously enabled rules; it does not grant new permission. Ordinary artifact links and recorded history remain available.

Artifacts and references with an integration appear as individual pills above the input. Enter or Space on a main pill opens an input-width details panel above the pills without moving the conversation or draft. The selected pill has a highlighted border. Details show the linked title, state icon and up to three lines of the actual description. Copy Link and Remove Artifact appear in the footer. Left and Right Arrow, Home and End select a list tab. Clicking a tab focuses its first item; arrow keys navigate list rows and Enter opens an item. A pill's status section selects and focuses the corresponding list or action, including when already open. Lists show single-line rows, with full text available in hovers and the Accessible View. Actions below the lists run once; enabled actions come first in provider order, with the first action primary. Inapplicable actions are hidden and blocked actions explain why. Autopilot groups automatic rules below the lists, with an Activities card below it when history exists. Both cards start collapsed and remember expansion. Autopilot switches grant standing permission and may run immediately when conditions hold. Saved rules remain revocable while unavailable. Turning a rule off prevents new runs but does not cancel work already started. Some activity rows reveal their related chat message; others are informational. Clicking another artifact switches the panel. Clicking the active pill, Escape or Close dismisses it. Escape and Close restore pill focus; outside clicks dismiss without moving focus back. Use Tab and Shift+Tab between controls, Space to change a switch, and accessibility help or the Accessible View{0} to read the full content. Background prompts do not replace your draft, attachments or visible chat.

Artifact details remember the selected list tab when closed and reopened. A tab can offer an information icon; hover it or focus it and press Enter or Space to read the provider's explanation without changing tabs. The Comments tab describes which review comments it includes.

When an artifact needs authentication, open its details and use Tab to reach Sign In. Enter or Space starts authentication in this window. The resource remains available from the linked title. Signing in does not enable automation.

Outside high contrast themes, use Set Background to choose no background, the built-in theme-aware Codicons pattern, a new image, or one of the five most recently selected images. One randomly selected icon in the Codicons pattern is a Celebrate button; press Tab to find it, then press Enter or Space to activate it. Each activation selects another random icon as the next Celebrate button. Use Change Background Layout to choose whether an image repeats, stretches, or appears at an edge or corner for the current color theme. Moving through the layout picker previews each option; select one to save it, or press Escape to restore the previous layout. Both commands are available from the Command Palette and by right-clicking empty chat space. Change Background Layout is shown only for images. Background customization is unavailable while a high contrast theme is active.

Press Shift+Tab from the chat input to reach metadata and status pills above it, use the left and right arrows to move between pills, and press Enter or Space to activate one. Live browsers appear in their own pill, and the chat's subagents appear in another. An aggregated pill opens a picker. Use Pin on a picker row to keep that entry as its own pill; it is removed from the picker, and a sole remaining entry is shown directly unless it requires a details picker. A pinned pill shows a trailing Unpin button that pointer users can activate to unpin it. Keyboard and screen reader users can open the pinned pill's context menu and choose Unpin. Pin choices are remembered for each chat. Subagents are grouped under Subagents: In Progress and Subagents: Completed. In Progress includes subagents waiting for input; Completed includes failed subagents. Use the up and down arrows to move between entries. When an entry has details, Tab moves through its row actions and detail links; Shift+Tab returns to the row action, and the up and down arrows continue moving between entries. Press Enter to open an entry, or Escape to dismiss the picker and return focus to the pill.

When a background image is set, use Tint Window to Match Background in the Command Palette or the background context menu to turn matching window colors on or off. A check mark means tinting is enabled. Turning it off keeps the background image and restores the original window colors.

Type /blobby to unlock True Name without sending a chat request. If Blobby is off, it turns on; if it is already on, the Color tab opens. Change Color in the pet's context menu always opens Color. Stable and Insiders are free choices; True Name unlocks solid and custom colors. Activating the True Name achievement card or account badge also opens Color. Use the color picker or enter an opaque hex color such as #ff8800, then activate Apply Color. Unapplied custom colors are discarded when you leave the tab or close the modal.

For a new Agent Host session in a Git repository, use Tab to reach the branch picker and press Enter or Space to choose a base branch. With New Worktree selected, the current branch's tracked upstream is selected by default when available; otherwise the default branch is selected. The picker lists the current branch's upstream and the current branch when it is not the default branch, then the default branch's remote-tracking branch and the default branch, then the other branches, with a separator between each group, and focuses the selected branch when it opens. Each branch is announced with its group name: Current Branch, Default Branch, or Branches. With Branch selected, the checked-out branch, which is the selected branch, is listed first when it is not the default branch, followed by the default branch in its own group, then the other branches. Use the arrow keys to choose a branch and press Enter to select it.

Available canvases appear in their own pill. A single canvas shows its title and opens directly; multiple canvases show a count and open a picker. Activating a canvas focuses its open tab or reopens it if it was closed. To close a canvas rather than only its tab, use Close Canvas: the X on a canvas pill or picker row, or the pill's context menu. Closing ends the canvas and notifies the extension that provides it.
Chats can be arranged in groups. Focus the previous group{0} or next group{1}. Split the active chat into a group to the right{2} or below{3}, or move it to the previous group{4} or next group{5}.

In both single and multiple tab layouts, sub-sessions in separate panes show their title followed by a dot and parent context as a secondary description, like editor tabs. This includes panes split within the parent session and panes positioned independently in the window. Sub-sessions sharing their parent's tab strip show only their title. Drag a sub-session tab or header outside its parent area to place that chat independently beside another session, without moving its parent. The chat keeps its original parent relationship. Closing the parent pane leaves independent sub-session panes open. You can drag a sub-session from the sidebar into the grid while its parent pane is closed. In multiple tab mode, drop it onto its parent's tab strip to reattach it as a tab, without creating a split. The parent's tab strip stays visible while a sub-session is detached. In single tab mode, detached sub-sessions cannot be dropped back into their parent panel. You can also use the split and move chat commands described above; session grid navigation and movement commands operate on the focused independent pane.

When the current environment and harness support chatting without a workspace, hover over or focus the workspace picker to reveal Chat without a workspace. Use Tab or the Left and Right arrow keys to reach this button, then Enter or Space to switch to Chat without discarding your prompt. You can send without choosing a workspace. Focus returns to the workspace picker so you can choose a workspace later. Chat remains available in the workspace list.
Activate a chat tab's close button to close (hide) that chat from the tab strip without deleting it; reopen it later from the Chats menu. The session's main chat cannot be closed.

When multiple session panes are visible, move focus to a pane header and activate Close to remove that pane from the grid. Closing a pane keeps the session and its worktree available in the Sessions list.

If cloud session creation or connection fails, the error notification offers Show Details. Focus the notification, then use Tab to reach Show Details and Enter or Space to open a dialog with the failed step and available request details. Opening details does not sign in or retry the request.

After you successfully use the suggestion to archive or mark a session as done three times, future suggestions appear in a compact layout without the explanation. The buttons wrap below the title when space is limited, while Dismiss stays at the top right. The keyboard order is Archive or Mark as Done, Configure, then Dismiss. Configure opens the same automatic cleanup settings.

When space is limited, the new-session pickers show icons instead of labels without moving to another row. The workspace name remains visible. Icon-only pickers retain their accessible names and tooltips; activate them to view and change the current selection.

In the new-session input, open the model picker and activate Compare Models. In Attempts, check two to ten distinct models. Attempts inherit the current workspace, branch, agent, and permissions. Done and Next stay disabled until two to ten models are checked, and the footer shows how many are selected. Use Tab to reach Done and Next. In Judge, optionally select a model to review the attempts and recommend a winner. Leave Judge unselected and activate Done to run attempts without review. With a Judge selected, activate Next to choose an optional Synthesizer. Without a Synthesizer, review is available but synthesis is not. Activate a selected model again to clear it. Back preserves your choices. Done returns to the composer; activate Run N Attempts to launch. Escape closes the picker without launching. Open the comparison parent in the Sessions list to open every available attempt in a resizable grid. With two attempt panes, both chat inputs remain visible. With three or more, only the active attempt pane shows its chat input; focus another attempt pane to show its input. Screen-reader optimized mode keeps every attempt input visible. After the Judge finishes, its chat shows a scorecard: the winning model with the Judge's explanation, then a row for each attempt, recommended first, with a summary of its validation checks such as Tests passed or Not run, total time, and tokens. Use Tab to reach the Checks column header to hear what the checks cover. Focus the comparison result and use Open Accessible View{0} to read its verdict and attempt metrics as plain text. Use Tab to reach the attempt rows and Up Arrow or Down Arrow to move between them, then press Enter or Space to expand a row with the Judge's reasoning, what is worth keeping, gaps, each check's result, and Open Attempt N. Each row also has an Open button after its metrics that opens that attempt's session. Activate Open Attempt to open the recommended attempt, or use its adjacent dropdown to open another attempt. When synthesis is available, Synthesize starts the Judge's default plan. Open its More Actions menu and choose Additional Synthesis Instructions to enter requirements that are remembered and applied to recommended synthesis. Activate Start Synthesis with Instructions, or press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) in that field, to start the recommended plan with those requirements. The additional instructions guide a new synthesis session and do not modify the original attempts.
Comparison selections are kept while draft permissions or mode are updating. Run N Attempts is unavailable until the update finishes.

The model picker offers Compare Models in the tab bar. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to begin setup. Use Compare Models{0} from the new-session input or model picker to open comparison setup directly. Enable the experimental sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint setting to also show Send Query to Multiple Models at the bottom with your configured shortcut until you first open comparison setup. The tab-bar toggle remains available to return to single-model selection.

In a Chat with no workspace, comparisons run the prompt in separate workspace-less chats. Select at least two attempts, activate Done, then Run N Attempts to compare their responses side by side. Folderless comparisons do not offer Judge or Synthesizer steps.

Use the comparison header's Mark All as Done action to mark its sessions done, with the same confirmation and Undo as other groups. When every participant is done, the automatically created group is removed. Undo restores the group and its sessions. Delete Group remains available from the comparison header context menu.

When a question tool needs attention in an inactive visible pane, the confirmation notification setting can show an operating system notification even while another pane in the Agents window is active.

The initial Judge and synthesis messages are collapsed under Judge Instructions or Synthesis Instructions. Use Tab to reach the summary, then press Enter or Space to expand or collapse the full instructions. The complete instructions remain in the conversation and in its Accessible View.

Attempts open in a grid when they start by default. Turn off sessions.chat.compareAgents.openInGrid to start them without automatic navigation. You can still select the comparison group to open its grid.
Judge results identify candidates as Attempt N with agent, model, and effort, then present Why it won in this order: Solution, Comparison, Validation, Code quality.

Comparison setup is a working copy until you activate Done. Escape or clicking outside the picker discards setup changes and keeps your previous single-model or configured comparison ready to send. Unfinished setup does not resume when you reopen the picker. Done commits your choices and changes the model label to N Attempts and Send to Run N Attempts. Reopening a configured comparison starts a working copy of those choices.
Running a comparison uses tokens for each session. The Run N Attempts button shows this warning immediately on hover.
While connecting to a Dev Container for an existing session, use Tab to reach Show Log and press Enter to open the Dev Container output channel.

When the new-session prompt contains known connector URLs, the standard chat tip can suggest matching connector tasks. Connector recommendations follow the same tip setting, eligibility, layout, navigation, and session visibility rules as other chat tips. No connector recommendation appears without a matching URL. When multiple connectors match, use the Previous Tip and Next Tip actions to browse every recommendation. Use Tab and Shift+Tab to reach the linked suggestion and the tip actions. Activate the link to review that connector in the Copilot Connectors marketplace. Dismissing the tip hides tips for the current session and prevents future URL-driven recommendations for that connector during this composer session.

Type # in the chat input to attach context. Use #file to reference a file or folder, or #session to reference another agent session. Referencing a session together with the /troubleshoot command analyzes that session's logs instead of the current one. Accept a suggestion with Tab or Enter. Openable references appear as buttons above the input; activate one to open it, or use its Remove button to detach it.

Chats open directly in the session view without a tab row. Side-by-side chats each show a session header. Pin keeps that chat visible when another chat opens. Close removes that chat group. Closing the last group closes the session from the grid. Non-main chats are hidden and can be reopened later. For sessions that support multiple chats, use Show Chat Tabs in the session overflow menu to show multiple tabs.

When multiple chats appear as tabs in a single group, the tab row replaces the session header and includes the session actions. Side-by-side chat groups retain the session header and keep their tab rows compact. For sessions that support multiple chats, use Show Chat Tabs in the session overflow menu to show a single chat.
To copy a browser link that opens an Agent Host session in the Agents window, open the session's context menu and choose Copy Link.

When a pill represents a single item, its context menu offers the item's copy actions, such as copying its URL or file path. For a collection, open the dropdown and use the individual row actions instead.

When a session was created by another session, focus it in the Sessions list and use the Show Hover command{0}. Move focus to the Created by link, then press Enter or Space to open the creator session.
Focus Chat Customizations in the left sidebar{0}.
Messages sent by another session or chat show a source annotation above the message. Press Tab to focus the annotation, then press Enter or Space to open the source chat.

Before a new nested session is committed, its session header and Sessions list row offer Delete without confirmation. After it is committed, those controls offer Archive or Mark as Done instead. To permanently delete a committed nested session, open the chat tab's context menu and choose Delete Chat. This is destructive and cannot be undone.
For a Cloud sandbox session, Delete removes its task and stored conversation even when the environment is offline. A failed deletion leaves the session in the list.
To permanently delete a session, open its context menu and choose Delete. This is destructive and cannot be undone.
To create an independent sub-session pane without dragging, focus the sub-session and run Detach Chat into New Pane{0} from the Command Palette. The new pane stays open when its parent pane closes.

When Dev Container Agent Host sessions are enabled, Docker is available on the host, and a local, SSH, Tunnel, or WSL folder contains a Dev Container configuration, open the folder's submenu and choose Use Dev Container. For remote folders, first connect to a host that supports Dev Container sessions. For WSL folders, Docker must be available in the WSL distribution. Use the arrow keys to navigate submenus and Enter to select. The workspace picker then identifies the folder with a Dev Container suffix. Choose Use This Computer or Use Remote Host to switch back.

The workspace picker includes Dev Container Sample. Open its submenu and choose a sample with the arrow keys and Enter. Selecting a sample does not start Docker or clone the repository. The sample is prepared in a Docker volume when you send your first prompt.

When dictation is configured, dictate your message into the input{0}. Tap to start and stop, or hold to dictate only while pressed. If the speech-to-text model is still preparing, activate the dictation control again to cancel.

The Left and Right arrow keys also reach disabled session controls, such as Copilot when Cloud is selected, so you can inspect their current value. Disabled controls cannot be activated and are skipped by Tab.

To mark an individual nested chat as done without marking its session as done, open the chat's context menu in the Sessions list or chat tab and choose Mark as Done. The chat is hidden from the Sessions list and closed, but is not deleted. Open the Sessions list Filter menu and enable Done to show it again, then open the chat's context menu and choose Restore.

When all GitHub pull requests associated with the session have merged and no chat is working or waiting for input, a mark as done suggestion may appear above the chat input. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Mark as Done, Configure Automatic Cleanup, or Dismiss Mark as Done Suggestion, then Enter or Space to activate it. Configure Automatic Cleanup opens the settings for automatically archiving inactive merged sessions and permanently deleting automatically archived merged sessions. The explanation under What Does "Mark as Done" Do? is collapsed by default. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Dismiss Mark as Done Suggestion, or Escape while the suggestion is focused, hides the suggestion for this session, including after a reload, until it is marked as done or deleted, and returns focus to the chat input. Marking the session as done hides it from the sessions list so you can focus on your remaining tasks. The session is not deleted. Ask your agent to find it, or look in the "Done" section of the sessions list. You can restore it anytime. The worktree created for the session, if any, will be deleted. You can recreate it by restoring the session.

When the side panel's editor has no open tabs, it shows Add Tab at the top and lists the Add Tab actions, such as Changes, Files, Browser, and Search, with their keybindings. Press Tab to reach the list, use the Up and Down arrow keys to move between actions, and press Enter or Space to open one. For an action with a submenu, such as Canvas, press Enter, Space, or the Right arrow key to open the submenu, the Up and Down arrow keys to choose an item, and the Left arrow key or Escape to return to the list.

Choose Environments in the workspace picker to connect to a GitHub environment, then select a folder on that host. The picker starts in the host's home directory. Enter a folder path to browse another location or drive. Use the arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select, and Escape to cancel either picker.

Choose This Computer, Cloud, a remote host, or an available Dev Container. Workspace and Session Type choices follow the selected environment. Local folders default to This Computer unless you explicitly choose or restore another environment. Choose Workspace is shown when no workspace is selected. Cloud uses Copilot. Dev Container lists only supported folders and requires a workspace; it does not fall back to Chat. Compare Agents is unavailable when Dev Container is selected. An incompatible workspace is cleared without sending or discarding your prompt. Use Tab or the Left and Right arrow keys to reach Environment, Enter or Space to open it, arrow keys and Enter to select, and Escape to dismiss. Screen-reader optimized mode keeps session options expanded.
Above the new-session input, Environment is before Workspace and remains visible when session options are collapsed.

Choose Manage at the bottom of the Environment picker to open the Remotes dialog and manage remote environments. This does not change your selected environment. Hosts not listed in Remotes, including configured WebSocket hosts, keep their per-entry Manage submenu.

Extension-provided artifact actions and automation use the same controls and request cards. Their automatic prompts go to the chat that recorded the artifact. Extension automation runs on this computer while the extension and session connection are available. Hosts without support for automation notices pause automatic actions and explain why; manual actions remain available. A rule can prevent a new schedule while allowing an existing schedule to continue. You can still use Space on its switch to turn it off.
Once you send a message to an external session's agent, it becomes a regular session. Its banner disappears, and it is no longer grouped or filtered as external.

When you first open a session created in another application, a banner appears at the top of the chat. Use Tab to reach its external-session picker, choose an option, and activate Save. The Close action dismisses the banner without changing the setting. Saving or closing permanently dismisses the banner.

When you first open a session created in another application, a banner explains that you can continue it here. Codex sessions can use your ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, selected in the model picker. Claude sessions use your Copilot subscription. Use Tab to reach Close and press Enter or Space to permanently dismiss the banner for all external sessions and return focus to the chat input.

The Sessions list Filter Sessions menu includes a Created Externally submenu. Choose None, Recent, Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, or Last 30 Days to control which sessions from other applications are shown. Last 7 Days is the default. Show in External Section places these sessions in their own External section. This option is off by default, so external sessions appear alongside other sessions in their normal groups.

To make an external session a regular session without sending a message, use Import in its row toolbar, before Archive or Mark as Done, or focus the session and choose Import from its context menu{0}. This action is available when the host supports importing sessions.

External sessions appear in an External section above Archived unless they are pinned or in a custom group. The section is hidden when empty. Focus its heading and open the context menu{0} to configure which external sessions are shown or archive the section's sessions.

External sessions appear in an External section above Done unless they are pinned or in a custom group. The section is hidden when empty. Focus its heading and open the context menu{0} to configure which external sessions are shown or mark the section's sessions as done.
When a session pull request has failing checks, use Reveal in its banner item to open that pull request, or use Fix Checks to ask the agent to address the failures.

When a feedback comments attachment appears above the input, focus it and press Enter or Space. A single comment opens directly. Multiple comments open a tree grouped by file; use the arrow keys to navigate, Enter to reveal a comment, and Escape to close the tree.

When pull requests have failing checks or unreviewed comments, one banner appears above the input. If several pull requests need attention, use the Previous Banner and Next Banner buttons to move between them. A pull request with both failing checks and comments uses a split button. Activate the main action to address both. Open its More Actions menu to choose Fix Checks or Address Comments separately. Choose Reveal Checks in the More Actions menu to open the pull request. Choose Reveal Comments in the same menu to view the first comment. In-product agent review comments appear as their own carousel item.

While the {0} setting is enabled, pull request failing-check and review-comment banners do not appear above the input. Open a recorded pull request artifact's details to review its checks and comments. In-product agent review comments still appear in a banner above the input.
To search the chat transcript, invoke Find in Chat{0}. Find Next{1} and Find Previous{2} move between results, scrolling each one into view.
Focus the active session{0}. The default Open Chat (Agent) shortcut also focuses the active session in the Agents window.

Alt-click, or Option-click on macOS, the Fork Conversation button at a checkpoint to open the fork beside its source. Ordinary activation keeps its existing behavior. With the keyboard, activate Fork Conversation, reopen the source from the Sessions list, then choose Open to the Side from the fork's context menu.

Generated images from this chat automatically appear in the Generated Images section of the Artifacts pill, separate from other images and files. When Images Preview is enabled for chat, open an image and use the Left and Right Arrow keys to browse generated images and user attachments from the conversation. Images shown from the transcript do not offer Remove from Session unless they were also recorded as artifacts.

Each consecutive batch of image-generation calls has its own preview in conversation order. Select any thumbnail, including one still generating, to show its image or progress and its tool dropdown above the preview. Use Tab to focus the selected thumbnail, then Left or Right Arrow, Home, or End to select another image or its progress. Expand the selected tool dropdown to inspect its prompt and output. The selected thumbnail has a highlighted border. The thumbnail row follows the selected preview's size. Generating images show only the compact glyph band, while cancelled or failed images show their status in the tool dropdown without an empty preview. The Image batch status below the thumbnails shows how many images are ready out of the total, along with any that need attention, failed, or were cancelled. Later results arrive without changing your selection, and only the selected preview animates. Focus the main image and press Enter to open the carousel. Approval and authentication requests remain visible even when another image is selected.

Use the download action beside the Image batch status to save all currently ready images as a ZIP archive. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to download. The action is unavailable until an image is ready and while a download is in progress. Only images ready when you start the download are included; failed, cancelled, and pending images are not included.

Expand a completed image-generation dropdown to inspect its duration, total image byte size, and tokens. A dash means the value was not reported; token usage is not yet available. Generated image downloads include a stable hash suffix so different images have distinct filenames.

Image-generation tool entries, previews, and batch counts stay hidden while the model assembles the tool arguments. If approval is required, the confirmation is the first tool UI shown. Generating image, the glyph animation, painting progress phrases, and the painting pet start only when the tool executes, after any required confirmation. Confirmation and authentication waits pause image-generation progress.
Use Add Context to attach files, images, and, when available, GitHub issues or pull requests.

Pull request and issue pills above the chat input open their GitHub item in the GitHub Pull Requests extension when it is available. Pills that represent several items open a keyboard-accessible picker.
Go back through visited sessions, the New Session view, and custom views such as Automations{0}.
Go forward through visited sessions and views{0}. Reopening New Session or a custom view moves its single history entry to the most recent position.

Custom groups, workspace groups, repository groups, and environment groups, including remote hosts, offer Change Icon and Change Color in their context menus. In the icon picker, enter a name to search, then press Down Arrow to enter the grid. Arrow keys navigate icons, Home and End move to the first and last icon, and Up Arrow from the top row returns to search. Tab and Shift+Tab move between search, the grid, and Reset to default. Press Enter to select an icon or reset. The color picker uses the terminal's theme-aware ANSI colors. Both pickers offer Reset to default, which resets only that part of the group's appearance. Escape cancels either picker without changing the group. Icon and color choices are saved independently for each group, including subgroups. Collapsed groups still show unread and attention indicators when needed.

After you switch from Copilot to Local, a feedback survey may appear above the chat input. Use Shift+Tab to reach it. Use Up and Down Arrow to choose why you switched, then press Enter or Space to submit. Dismiss Survey or Escape closes the survey. After submission, a message confirms that your feedback was recorded. Use Tab to reach Share it on GitHub to provide specific feedback in a GitHub issue. Use Dismiss Feedback Acknowledgement or Escape to close the message.
Use up and down arrows to navigate your request history in the input box.

Previously loaded conversations refresh silently. If recent messages cannot be loaded, a banner offers Refresh. Use Tab to reach Refresh and press Enter or Space to retry loading recorded messages without restarting the session or waking its environment. Your draft is preserved.

Images Preview offers Download for the selected image. Image rows in Artifacts and References offer Download Image. Use Tab to reach these actions and Enter or Space to download. When a pill contains a single image, its download action is also available in the pill hover and context menu. Opening an image in the new-session composer includes all images attached to that draft.
You are in the chat input. Type a message and press Enter to send it.
Press Alt+Enter to start the session in the background without navigating into it. The started session appears in the Chat Sessions view.

When session metadata or active-turn status pills appear above the input, press Shift+Tab to reach them, use the Left and Right arrow keys to move between them, and press Enter or Space to activate one. Open the context menu{0} to choose which pills are shown. Pull Requests Options lets you show all pull requests or only open and draft ones. Subagent Options offers Show All and Show In Progress. These choices are remembered across sessions. If every entry of a pill is filtered out, its options are also available in any other pill's context menu or the toolbar context menu.

Choose Default or Compact from View > Appearance > Layout Density, or change the window.density.layout setting. Default uses a taller title bar. Compact uses a shorter title bar, removes the gaps between parts, and reduces pane spacing. Changes apply immediately.
To open the main chat beside a peer chat, choose Open to the Side from the session row's context menu. You can also Alt-click (Option-click on macOS) the row or drag it to a chat pane's edge.
The same read and unread shortcuts work on nested sessions and change only the targeted nested sessions, not their parent.
When a parent session has unread nested sessions, open its context menu and choose Mark All as Read.
When the Sessions list has focus, mark the focused session or selected sessions as read{0} or unread{1} without opening them. These shortcuts do not apply while typing in an input.
To choose a microphone or turn off dictation or Voice Mode, focus the microphone button in the input toolbar and open its context menu (for example Shift+F10).

When agent customizations need an update, a notice below the new-session input shows how many need attention. Use Tab to reach Review Migrations and open the Migrations page. Dismiss Migration Notice for This Workspace hides the notice for that workspace, including after restarting, and returns focus to the input.

In Manage Remote Agent Hosts or the workspace picker, choose Environments to discover your environments without starting compute or sessions. Use the arrow keys to choose an environment and Enter to connect. Tab reaches Refresh Environments. Escape returns to the previous control. Environment options offer Reconnect, Disconnect, and Rename. Rename changes only this profile's label, not the remote machine's name. The picker shows whether each environment is online or offline and whether you are connected to it.
On mobile, the mode and model pickers appear as tappable chips below the input. Tap a chip to open a bottom sheet where you can change the selection.

To reorder a session's nested chats in the Sessions list, focus a nested chat and invoke Move Up{0} or Move Down{1}, or choose them from its context menu. They are available only for nested chats that their provider can move. Focus stays on the moved chat.

When a chat tab is focused, use the left and right arrow keys to move to and activate an adjacent chat tab, or Home and End to activate the first and last tabs. Tabs that do not fit are scrolled into view when activated. You can also scroll the tab row with the mouse wheel or drag the horizontal scrollbar that appears when hovering over overflowing tabs.
Navigate to the next session in the list{0}.
Navigate to the previous session in the list{0}.

Custom groups can contain subgroups at any depth. Focus a group's heading and open the context menu{0} to choose Create Subgroup, which adds an empty group inside it and starts renaming it. Subgroups are listed above the group's own sessions, and each group's level is announced. Mark All as Done and Mark All as Read on a group include its subgroups' sessions. Delete Group also deletes the group's subgroups; when it deletes more than one group, an Undo notice appears at the bottom of the Sessions list that restores them. Create Group on sessions that are all in the same group creates the new group inside it.

Workspace, repository, and environment sections can also be placed inside custom groups. Focus a section heading and open the context menu{0}, then choose Move to Group and a destination. Remove from Group returns it to the top level. You can also drag the section heading into a custom group or beside another header. The section includes future matching sessions, while pinned sessions and explicit custom-group memberships keep their placement. Section nesting is remembered separately for each grouping mode and is hidden when another mode is selected. Group actions include the sessions of their currently nested sections. Deleting a custom group returns its nested sections to the top level and offers an Undo notice that restores their placement.

New Nested Session{0} opens a composer that uses the session's agent and host, so it has no agent or environment picker. Above the input, the folder picker preselects the session's folder, or No Workspace in a session without one. When the session's folder no longer exists, No Workspace is preselected and the picker says why. Pick a recent folder, browse or open a folder, or pick No Workspace to give the nested chat its own scratch folder. For a Git folder, check New Worktree to give the nested chat its own worktree and pick the branch it starts from. An agent that supports only one folder offers only the session's folder. The choice applies when you send the first request.

When a subagent starts another subagent, its activity row identifies the nested subagent by name. Focus that link with Tab and press Enter or Space to open the nested subagent's chat beside the current chat. The enclosing pill still opens the parent subagent.
To move a new-session pane before sending a prompt, drag its blank top area beside another pane. The session grid movement commands also work on new-session panes.

When an Agent picker is available in a new or running session, it initially appears in Add Context. Open Add Context and choose Agent to select an agent. After you select an agent, the Agent picker returns to its usual position. Other new-session controls remain in their layout-specific positions. Use Tab to reach toolbar controls, arrow keys to navigate toolbar items, and Enter or Space to open a picker.

Inside the new-session prompt, the controls appear in this order: Add Context, Agent, Mode and Permissions, and Model. Which controls are available depends on the selected harness. Use Tab to reach the controls, arrow keys to navigate toolbar items, and Enter or Space to open a picker.

Inside the new-session prompt, Add Context and Model appear in the input toolbar. Agent, Mode, and Permissions appear below the input when available for the selected harness. Use Tab to reach the controls, arrow keys to navigate toolbar items, and Enter or Space to open a picker.
In a new-session composer, open and focus the workspace picker{0} or the harness picker{1}. Focus either picker control and open its context menu{2} to configure its keybinding.

By default, opening a cloud sandbox conversation connects or wakes its environment in the background. Turn off chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.autoConnectOnOpen to wait until you start composing or explicitly connect instead. You can read its history and compose a draft while it connects. Connection progress and failures appear in a banner only after you type, paste, or add an attachment. If the session is ready before you start composing, no connection banner appears. Send, mode, and permissions are unavailable until the session is ready. If connecting fails, your draft stays in the input; use Retry in the banner to try again. Connecting never sends your draft automatically.

When the session is associated with GitHub pull requests, a status pill above the chat input shows the pull request number or count. Activate it to open a single pull request or choose from the associated pull requests{0}.

You are in the Agents window. The Agents window is a dedicated workspace for working with AI agents. It provides a chat interface, a changes view for reviewing agent-generated changes, a file explorer, and customization options.
To paste the clipboard as plain text, without converting it to Markdown or storing it as an attachment, invoke Paste as Text{0}.
Long pasted text is stored as an attached text item and replaced in the input with a numbered inline reference.
To choose a folder from a searchable list instead, use the New Session in Folder command{0}.

While the new-session input has focus, open the environment picker{0}, branch picker{1}, or Branch/New Worktree picker{2}. Focus Sync Changes{3}, then press Enter to synchronize. These shortcuts are available only when the corresponding control is available and expand hidden session options before focusing them.

If your organization disables Claude or Codex and requires the new Copilot experience, an open, idle conversation automatically moves to Copilot with its title, history, and draft. Nothing is sent automatically. The original is archived only after the copy opens and other conversations in its session can still be reached. Opening an archived original does not move it again. If moving needs a workspace or trust decision, or fails, use Tab to focus Continue in Copilot in the banner, then press Enter or Space. This action reopens an existing copy when available. Subagent chats and other policy restrictions use the manual action. For a managed checkout, choose an independent workspace; uncommitted files stay in the original checkout.

Focus Session 1 in Grid{0} and the other numbered focus commands follow visual pane order, including independent sub-session panes even when their parent is closed. Focus Last Session in Grid{1} selects the last pane.

While a new session is being prepared, the transcript shows your submitted prompt and attachments followed by startup progress. Use Tab to reach Show Log beside the progress message and press Enter to open the Dev Container output channel. The chat input and attachment controls are disabled until preparation finishes. Use the input's Stop action or Cancel Chat command{0} to cancel preparation. If preparation fails or is canceled, your original prompt and attachments remain in the new-session composer.

When prompt options appear above the new-session input, use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between them, then press Enter or Space to insert one. You can select a different option while the input is empty, exactly matches the inserted prompt, or only has its editable placeholder removed; other edits disable the options without hiding them. Clearing the input also clears the selected option. Use the Close action to hide the options and return focus to the input.
When the new-session prompt contains a highlighted task placeholder, place the caret inside it and replace it{0} to type your task.

When the prompt timeline is enabled, a handle on the left edge of the transcript lists your prompts. Activate it to expand the list, use the up and down arrows (or Home and End) to move between prompts, Enter or Space to jump to a prompt, and Escape to dismiss the list and return focus to the handle. When a prompt title is pinned above the transcript, activate its title to jump to that prompt.

Recorded GitHub pull request artifacts can show checks and unresolved review threads as additional pill sections. Their details offer repair actions and separate, opt-in automation controls. Repair prompts require a matching checkout and instruct the agent to commit and push the repair. Automatically Mark Ready can exclude check-name patterns configured in Settings; automatic merging still requires every check to pass. The main details offer Mark Ready, Merge, and branch-update controls. Branch-discovered pull requests and reference links do not gain these automations.

In a repository section where New Session is a split button, focus New Session and press Right Arrow to reach its dropdown, then activate New Session from Pull Request to open a searchable pull request picker. Pull requests are grouped by review and assignment status. Use the arrow keys to navigate, Enter to create the session, and Escape to close the picker.

To start a workspace-less quick chat, use the New Quick Chat command{0} or the plus button on the Chats section in the sessions list. When consolidated remote workspaces are enabled, this opens the new-session composer, where you can choose Chat. Otherwise, it starts a workspace-less chat directly. When GitHub sandboxes are enabled, choose Cloud in the Environment picker, then Chat in the workspace picker, to chat without a repository or pull request. If the Environment picker is disabled, choose Cloud in the harness picker instead. The Toggle Side Panel command is disabled for quick chats.

Quick chats can have nested chats: use New Nested Session{0} on a quick chat, and each nested chat works in its own scratch folder. Chats move between quick chats and workspace sessions and keep their folder. A quick chat stays in the Chats section, and those of its chats that have a folder of their own announce it. A chat that shares its folder with another chat in its session can't be moved on its own.

On desktop, the title bar offers Remote Connections. The preview setting chat.agentHost.remoteConnections selects the connection method. The Remote Connections button opens a menu that offers Off, Dev Tunnels, and GitHub Environments when available. Use Tab to reach the title bar, arrow keys to reach the button, Enter or Space to open it, Up and Down Arrow to choose an option, Enter to select, and Escape to close and return focus to the button. Selecting a method updates the setting and enables sharing. Selecting Off disables sharing without changing the preferred method. The footer shows the name used to identify this machine on other clients and whether it is shared or connecting. Changing the setting directly turns sharing off. The setting chat.agentHost.githubEnvironments.enabled controls GitHub Environments availability. If your organization disables it, the menu explains that you must contact your administrator. With GitHub environment selected, enabling sharing registers your local environment for remote owner access and allows clients authenticated as your GitHub account to read and modify files across this machine's accessible file systems, including sensitive files. Remote work uses the host's OAuth token by default, controlled by chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.useLocalCredentials. Operating system permissions still apply. Local sessions continue using local IPC.

If GitHub Environments is disabled by your organization, the footer explains the restriction. Press Tab to reach View Setting and Enter to open the managed setting. Shift+Tab returns to the connection options.

In the Remote Connections menu, press Tab to reach the name link in the footer, then Enter or Space to rename the shared environment. The input starts with the current name. Enter saves the name shown on other clients, and Escape cancels. Shift+Tab returns to the connection options. Renaming while Off does not enable sharing.

Ask the agent to list remote agent hosts or create a remote session with platform and resource requirements. Creation uses the standard tool confirmation and does not change the focused chat. The result includes a link to the remote session. Remote sessions can send messages back to the originating chat while this Agents window remains connected.

Ask the agent to inspect a remote session using its session link. Inspection reads its current state and latest response or error without changing focus, marking the chat as read, or approving pending requests. If the host is unavailable, the result explains why; inspection does not reconnect it.

Recorded artifacts and references offer Remove from Session for each row. Use Tab to reach row actions. When only one item is visible, use its pill hover actions or context menu instead. Removal waits for persistence and only deletes the session record; it does not delete the linked resource, close a pull request or issue, or remove independent session associations.

Workspace rows offer a Remove action. Use the arrow keys to focus a workspace, then Tab to reach its actions. Removed workspaces stay hidden across reloads until you browse to that workspace and successfully start a session from the new-session composer. Removing a workspace does not delete its sessions or files.

When Rename is available for a non-main chat, focus its tab or nested row in the Sessions list and invoke Rename{0}, or double-click its title, to rename it inline. Type the new title, then press Enter to confirm or Escape to cancel. From the chat transcript or input, invoking Rename opens a prompt instead.

To rename a session inline, focus its row in the Sessions list and invoke Rename{0}, double-click its title, or open its context menu and choose Rename. Type the new title, then press Enter to confirm or Escape to cancel. From the main chat transcript or input, invoking Rename edits the header title inline when it is visible and opens a prompt otherwise.

If the environment is connected but the conversation cannot be reopened, the banner offers Retry. Use Tab to reach Retry and press Enter or Space to reopen the conversation on the existing connection. The banner reports reopening progress and offers Retry again if it fails. Your draft is preserved and is not sent automatically. Send stays unavailable until the conversation is ready.

This host creates a new environment for each session. Open Select Repository to choose its repository. Selecting a repository does not start an environment; sending your first message does. Before sending, use the mode picker to choose Interactive, Plan, or Autopilot, and the permissions picker to configure tool approvals. Open the model picker to choose a cloud model and its supported reasoning effort. Use the arrow keys to navigate options, Enter to select, and Escape to close a picker.

In a repository section with sessions in several environments, the New Session dropdown can start a session in each environment, in the workspace of its most recently created session there. Session rows in a repository section name their environment, except for This Computer.

When choosing a GitHub repository in the browser, search or enter a GitHub URL or owner/repository. Use the arrow keys to navigate results, Enter to select, and Escape to cancel. Sign in to GitHub if prompted.
When you select assistant response text, an Ask Question input appears. Type a side question and press Enter to send it, press Shift+Enter to insert a new line, or press Escape to dismiss the input.

When you select assistant response text, an action menu appears. Press Tab to focus the menu, use the Up Arrow and Down Arrow keys to move between actions, and press Enter to activate one. Press Escape to dismiss the menu. Ask in a Side Chat opens a question input anchored to the selected text. Quote appends the selection as a blockquote in the chat input when the conversation is interactive. Copy copies the selected text.

The Session Activity Bar beside the active chat opens the Changes, Files, Browser, and Canvas tabs. The pull request action appears automatically in the side-pane group. Open Pull Request is available for the active chat's pull requests when a contributed opener is available for their links. The action reveals an already-open matching editor or opens the first supported pull request if none is open. A checked button means the pull request editor is visible; activating it collapses the side pane. Activate it again to reveal the editor. The action opens directly, without a dropdown or picker, even with multiple pull requests. Issue actions are not shown in the activity bar; issue pills remain available above the chat input. Its layout actions, Toggle Side Panel above the tabs and Toggle Panel below them, replace the title bar buttons; turn them off with Show Layout Actions in its context menu. Press Tab past the chat input's controls to reach it, use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move between its entries, and press Enter or Space to open one. The Changes entry's label includes the active chat's number of changed files and lines added and removed, and New changes when it has changes you have not yet seen in the Changes tab. Only canvases belonging to the active chat are shown. A single canvas opens directly and is labeled with its title. With multiple canvases, Canvas opens a submenu: press Enter, Space, or Left Arrow to open it, and Right Arrow or Escape to close it. When the active chat has no canvases, Canvas instead opens a submenu, even with a single entry, listing the canvases you can open or reopen, the same entries as the Canvas submenu of the empty editor's Add Tab list. Open the context menu{1} on an entry to hide that entry or the whole activity bar. Toggle the activity bar from the chat background's context menu, View > Appearance > Session Activity Bar, or the {0} setting.

A session created outside VS Code names its application in the session hover. Focus the hover, then use Tab to reach Created in and Enter or Space to open Filter Sessions with Created In focused. Use Right Arrow to open that submenu. The application remains visible after the session becomes a regular session.

Created In lists the applications that created sessions, grouped by This Computer, Cloud, and each remote host, with the environment in each application's name. VS Code is always offered for each available environment, even before you create a session there. Other applications are listed after a session created in them is discovered. Only applications from included environments are listed. Excluding an environment hides its applications without changing their selections; including it again restores them. Other list filters do not remove application choices. Included remote hosts retain their applications while cached sessions remain, even when disconnected. If no environments are included, select an environment first.

The Environment, Created In, and Harness submenus filter the Sessions list. Checked options are included. On This Computer and remote hosts, applications other than VS Code are hidden by default. Slack and Teams applications in Cloud are also hidden by default. Show Done, or Show Archived depending on your settings, includes archived sessions. Reset Filters restores these defaults and shows an Undo notice at the bottom of the Sessions list that restores your previous filters. On desktop, Compact View and Collapse All Groups are available from the Sessions More Actions menu. On phone, use Sort and Find to navigate the list.

Session panes form a separate grid from the chat groups inside each session. Focus the session to the left{0}, right{1}, above{2}, or below{3}. The generic Navigate to the View on the Left{4}, Navigate to the View on the Right{5}, Navigate to the View Above{6}, and Navigate to the View Below{7} commands do the same while focus is in the session grid. The Session Layout menu and Command Palette offer Move Session Left, Right, Above, and Below, Increase or Decrease Session Width and Height, and Arrange Sessions in a Balanced Grid. Arranging preserves the conversations and does not change side panels. On a phone, only the active session is shown; returning to a wider window restores the desktop arrangement.

Above the new-session input, the workspace, repository and harness pickers are shown initially. As the chat narrows, picker labels are replaced by icons one at a time from right to left, except for the workspace name. Labels return when more space is available. Use Tab and Shift+Tab, or the Left and Right Arrow keys, to move between these controls. Press Enter or Space to open a picker, use the Up and Down Arrow keys to navigate its options, and press Escape to close it and return focus to its control. The isolation picker offers New Worktree to create a separate copy for the session, or Branch to work in the existing repository. The branch picker chooses the base branch for a new worktree or checks out a branch in the existing repository. Hide Session Options collapses these controls without changing your selections. Show Session Options or the Focus New Session Harness Picker command expands the controls again.

Above the new-session input, the workspace, repository and harness pickers are shown. As the chat narrows, picker labels are replaced by icons one at a time from right to left, except for the workspace name. Labels return when more space is available. Use Tab and Shift+Tab, or the Left and Right Arrow keys, to move between these controls. Press Enter or Space to open a picker, use the Up and Down Arrow keys to navigate its options, and press Escape to close it and return focus to its control. The isolation picker offers New Worktree to create a separate copy for the session, or Branch to work in the existing repository. The branch picker chooses the base branch for a new worktree or checks out a branch in the existing repository. These controls stay expanded while a screen reader is active.

On desktop, the Filter Sessions menu offers Ordering and Grouping submenus. Grouping by Repository lists the sessions of each GitHub repository together, whether they run on This Computer, in Cloud, or on a remote host. Sessions without a GitHub repository stay in their workspace section. Grouping by Environment lists sessions together under This Computer, Cloud, or their remote host, across agents and workspaces. When grouping by Workspace, Repository, or Environment, Show switches between Recent and All sessions. Current choices are checked inside the submenus. Use the Right arrow key to open a submenu, the Left arrow key to return, and Enter or Space to choose an option.
Open a nested chat's context menu to rename it, open it to the side, or, when supported, permanently delete it. Agent Host chats also offer Copy Link.

Sessions with multiple user-facing chats show those chats nested beneath the session in the Sessions list. Use the arrow keys to navigate the list and Enter to show a chat as the session view. Side chats and subagent chats are omitted from this nested list: side chats are reachable from the Side Chats dropdown in the session's overflow menu, and subagent chats open from their pills in the chat transcript.

Sessions with multiple user-facing chats show those chats nested beneath the session in the Sessions list. Use the arrow keys to navigate the list and Enter to open a chat as a tab. Side chats and subagent chats are omitted from this nested list: side chats are reachable from the Side Chats dropdown in the session's overflow menu, and subagent chats open from their pills in the chat transcript.
The session row toolbar offers Pin or Unpin before Archive. For sessions that support multiple chats, open the session's context menu to start a new chat.
The session row toolbar offers Pin or Unpin before Mark as Done. For sessions that support multiple chats, open the session's context menu to start a new chat.
For non-cloud sessions that support multiple chats, the session row toolbar offers New Nested Session before Archive. Open the session's context menu to pin or unpin it.
For non-cloud sessions that support multiple chats, the session row toolbar offers New Nested Session before Mark as Done. Open the session's context menu to pin or unpin it.
Use Archived in the Sessions list Filter menu to control whether archived sessions and nested chats are shown. A check mark means archived content is shown.
Use Done in the Sessions list Filter menu to control whether done sessions and nested chats are shown. A check mark means done content is shown.
Subagent pills announce their model settings when available. Use Tab to focus file and markdown links in the activity row, then Enter to open them independently of the subagent chat.

Activate a subagent pill in the chat transcript to open the subagent beside the current chat. With the keyboard, focus a pill and press Enter or Space; Alt+Enter also opens it to the side. You can also drag a pill to a chat group's edge to choose where it opens.

When available for a folder session with incoming or outgoing commits, Sync Changes appears with the commit counts in the same repository toolbar as the worktree and branch controls above the input. It is hidden when New Worktree is selected. Use Tab and the arrow keys to reach it, then Enter or Space to synchronize the session's repository. The action is disabled while synchronization is running.

When available for a folder session with incoming or outgoing commits, Sync Changes appears with the commit counts in the same repository toolbar as the worktree and branch controls below the input. It is hidden when New Worktree is selected. Use Tab and the arrow keys to reach it, then Enter or Space to synchronize the session's repository. The action is disabled while synchronization is running.
Toggle the side panel (the editor area together with the auxiliary bar) open or closed{0}.

Status pills above the chat input include the session's diff stats (lines added and removed). Activate the Changes pill to open the multi-file diff editor with Session Changes for a folder session or Branch Changes for a worktree session{0}.
Start or stop Voice Mode to interact with the agent using your microphone{0}.

Use the checked Pet item in the new-session view context menu, or type /vscode-pet, to show or hide the VS Code pet above the input. Drag it horizontally to reposition it, or use Tab to focus it and the left and right arrow keys to move it. Press Enter or Space to show it some love.

When the pet is enabled, the user account menu lists unlocked achievement badges before locked badges and provides a View Achievements button. A gold star on the pet announces a newly unlocked achievement; activate the pet while the star is visible to open Achievements.
While an image-generation tool is running, the pet paints at a small easel, then returns to its normal activity. Reduced motion shows a still painting pose.

On the web, the host picker includes Dev Tunnels and GitHub environments. Online GitHub environments connect automatically when {0} is enabled, so their sessions appear in the Sessions list. An explicit Disconnect keeps that environment disconnected until you connect it again. Use Tab to reach the host picker, Enter or Space to open it, and arrow keys and Enter to choose a host, Connect, Disconnect, or Re-discover Hosts. On phones, the Hosts sheet offers Re-discover hosts and Open Connection Information for connection controls.

In a new session, the welcome heading is announced when shown. To disable this announcement, set accessibility.verbosity.newSessionWelcome to false. Press Tab to reach Customize Welcome Message beside the welcome heading, or open its context menu{0}. Choose Name to enter a custom name, or clear it to use your GitHub first name when available. Choose Phrases to open the setting where you add or replace welcome phrases, using {1} to position the name.

Use Tab or Shift+Tab to navigate to the workspace picker and choose a workspace for your session. When consolidated remote workspaces are enabled, opening the picker focuses its search input so you can immediately type to filter workspaces. If quick chats are available, you can also choose No workspace to start a workspace-less chat.

Opening Agents from an editor can suggest that editor's folder for a fresh session. An already-open window keeps its active and visible sessions unless a session or New Session is explicitly requested. Revealing New Session preserves any unsent draft. Choosing a workspace yourself or starting another session cancels a pending suggestion. If an explicitly requested workspace cannot be selected, a notification offers Retry and Choose Workspace actions.

When at least 20 inactive session worktrees are eligible for cleanup or eligible inactive worktrees can reclaim at least 5 GiB, a storage suggestion may appear below the Sessions list and is announced with the Open Worktree Cleanup Command Palette command. The command is also available from the Sessions More Actions menu. Active, running, needs-input, pinned, and recently used sessions are excluded. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Open Worktree Cleanup, Don't Show Again, or Dismiss Session Storage Suggestion, then Enter or Space to activate it. Don't Show Again disables future suggestions and announcements across restarts. Press Escape while focus is in the suggestion to dismiss it for the current window. To stop these suggestions and announcements without using the suggestion itself, run Disable Session Storage Cleanup Suggestions from the Command Palette, or run Open Worktree Cleanup and clear the Suggest Cleaning Up Session Storage When It Grows Large checkbox.
